sentences.zh: 案《禹貢》為海岱之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。

translations.literal: According to the "Tribute of Yu," this is the land between the sea and Mount Tai; Shun established twelve regional shepherds, and this was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" places this belt between the eastern sea and Mount Tai among the twelve pastures Shun set over the realm—Qingzhou was one of those twelve.

sentences.zh: 舜以青州越海，又分為營州，則遼東本為青州矣。

translations.literal: Shun, because Qingzhou crossed the sea, again divided off Yingzhou—thus Liaodong was originally part of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shun split another province, Yingzhou, out of Qingzhou where its jurisdiction reached across the sea, which is why Liaodong was counted as Qingzhou in the first place.

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" states: "The due east is called Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" names the eastern quarter of the realm "Qingzhou."

sentences.zh: 」蓋取土居少陽，其色為青，故以名也。

translations.literal: " Presumably it takes the soil as dwelling in the lesser-yang position; its color is green, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: " The name reflects yin–yang lore: the sector sits in the lesser yang, whose associated color is green, so the province is called "Qing," the green quarter.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「虛危流為青州。

translations.literal: The "Yuanming Bao of the Spring and Autumn Annals" says: "Emptiness and Rooftop flow and become Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphon "Yuanming Bao" maps the lunar lodges Emptiness and Rooftop onto the land called Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」漢武帝置十三州，因舊名，歷後漢至晉不改。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu of Han established thirteen provinces, following the old name; through Later Han down to Jin it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wu of Han carved the realm into thirteen provinces, he kept the old Qingzhou label, and Later Han and Jin left that usage in place.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉喪亂，青州淪沒石氏。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia disaster and turmoil, Qingzhou sank and was lost to the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia debacle, Qingzhou fell entirely under the Later Zhao Shi regime.

translations.literal: Cao Yi of Donglai became inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi, a man of Donglai, took charge as provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 造廣固城，後為石季龍所滅。

translations.literal: He built Guanggu city; later he was destroyed by Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: He walled the fortress of Guanggu, only to be crushed later by Shi Jilong.

sentences.zh: 季龍末，遼西段龕自號齊王，據青州。

translations.literal: At the end of Jilong's time, Duan Kan of Liaoxi styled himself king of Qi and held Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shi Jilong's reign, Duan Kan from west of the Liao styled himself King of Qi and seized Qingzhou.

translations.literal: Murong Ke destroyed Zhao and took Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke's conquest of Later Zhao brought Qingzhou under Yan.

translations.literal: The Fu clan pacified Yan and wholly possessed its territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Former Qin overthrew Yan, Fu Jian's house absorbed every district.

sentences.zh: 及苻氏敗後，刺史苻朗以州降。

translations.literal: When the Fu clan was defeated thereafter, Inspector Fu Lang surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Former Qin collapsed, provincial inspector Fu Lang handed the region over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷置幽州，以別駕辟閭渾為刺史，鎮廣固。

translations.literal: The court established Youzhou, appointing chief clerk Pilu Hun as inspector and stationing him at Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court reconstituted the province—our text reads "Youzhou," though many editions say "Qingzhou"—and sent chief clerk Pilu Hun to Guanggu as inspector.

sentences.zh: ，為慕容德所滅，遂都之，是為南燕，復改為青州。

translations.literal: , he was destroyed by Murong De, who then made it his capital; this is Southern Yan, and again it was changed to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De overthrew Pilu Hun, chose Guanggu as his capital, and founded Southern Yan, once more styling the territory Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 德以并州牧鎮陰平，幽州刺史鎮發幹，徐州刺史鎮莒城，青州刺史鎮東萊，兗州刺史鎮梁父。

translations.literal: De stationed the governor of Bing at Yinping, the governor of You at Fagan, the governor of Xu at Ju city, the governor of Qing at Donglai, and the governor of Yan at Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De fanned his officers across the map: a Bing governor at Yinping, a You governor at Fagan, Xu at Ju, Qing at Donglai, and Yan at Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 慕容超移青州於東萊郡，後為劉裕所滅，留長史羊穆之為青州刺史，築東陽城而居之。

translations.literal: Murong Chao moved Qingzhou to Donglai commandery; later he was destroyed by Liu Yu, who left chief clerk Yang Muzhi as governor of Qingzhou, built Dongyang city, and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao shifted the Qingzhou seat into Donglai; when Liu Yu extinguished Southern Yan, he left Yang Muzhi as acting governor, who raised Dongyang city and lived there.

sentences.zh: 自元帝渡江，於廣陵僑置青州。

translations.literal: From the time Yuan Emperor crossed the river, a nominal Qingzhou was planted at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Rui crossed the Yangzi, the court maintained a refugee "Qingzhou" administration at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 至是始置北青州，鎮東陽城，以僑立州為南青州。

translations.literal: At this point Northern Qingzhou was first established, seated at Dongyang city, and the emigre province was called Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jin formalize a Northern Qingzhou based at Dongyang, while the older exile administration was labeled Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 而後省南青州，而北青州直曰青州。

translations.literal: Later Southern Qingzhou was abolished, and Northern Qingzhou was simply called Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qingzhou was later folded away, leaving the northern seat to bear the plain name Qingzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou

sentences.zh: 案《禹貢》海岱及淮之地，舜十二牧，則其一也。

translations.literal: According to the "Tribute of Yu," this is the land of sea, Dai, and the Huai; of Shun's twelve shepherds, it was one.
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" describes this belt as stretching from the sea and Mount Tai down to the Huai—another of Shun's twelve regional pastures.

translations.literal: In Zhou times it entered the territory of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou dynasty the same ground was reckoned part of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「天氐流為徐州。

translations.literal: The "Yuanming Bao of the Spring and Autumn Annals" says: "Celestial Base flows and becomes Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphon "Yuanming Bao" ties the Celestial Base lunar lodge to the province called Xu.

sentences.zh: 」蓋取舒緩之義，或云因徐丘以立名。

translations.literal: " Presumably it takes the meaning of ease and slackness; some say it was established from Xu Hill to make the name.
translations.idiomatic: " The name is explained as "easygoing" qi; another etymology traces it to Xu Mound.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，以置泗水、薛、琅邪三郡。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm and thereby established the three commanderies of Sishui, Xue, and Langya.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin unified China, it organized this ground as Sishui, Xue, and Langya commanderies.

translations.literal: At the Chu–Han transition, Dongyang commandery was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: During the struggle between Chu and Han, a separate Dongyang commandery was carved out.

sentences.zh: 漢又分置東海郡，改泗水為沛，改薛為魯，分沛置楚國，以東陽屬吳國。

translations.literal: Han again separately established Donghai commandery, changed Sishui to Pei, changed Xue to Lu, split Pei to establish the kingdom of Chu, and subordinated Dongyang to the kingdom of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Han added Donghai commandery, renamed Sishui as Pei and Xue as Lu, hived part of Pei off into the kingdom of Chu, and attached Dongyang to the kingdom of Wu.

sentences.zh: 景帝改吳為江都，武帝分沛、東陽置臨淮郡，改江都為廣陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing changed Wu to Jiangdu; Emperor Wu split Pei and Dongyang to establish Linhuai commandery, and changed Jiangdu to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Han renamed the old Wu kingdom Jiangdu; his successor Emperor Wu carved Pei and Dongyang into a new Linhuai commandery and redesignated Jiangdu as Guangling.

sentences.zh: 及置十三州，以其地為徐州，統楚國及東海、琅邪、臨淮、廣陵四郡。

translations.literal: When the thirteen provinces were established, this territory became Xuzhou, commanding the kingdom of Chu and the four commanderies of Donghai, Langya, Linhuai, and Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu drew the thirteen provinces, this belt became Xuzhou, overseeing the kingdom of Chu plus Donghai, Langya, Linhuai, and Guangling commanderies.

sentences.zh: 宣帝改楚為彭城郡，後漢改為彭城國，以沛郡之廣戚縣來屬，改臨淮為下邳國。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan changed Chu to Pengcheng commandery; Later Han changed it to the kingdom of Pengcheng, brought Guangqi county from Pei commandery into it, and changed Linhuai to the kingdom of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han turned the Chu kingdom into Pengcheng commandery; Later Han raised it to a kingdom again, folded in Guangqi from Pei, and converted old Linhuai into the kingdom of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 及，復分下邳屬縣在淮南者置臨淮郡，分琅邪置東莞郡。

translations.literal: When that time came, again those counties of Xiapi that lay south of the Huai were separated to establish Linhuai commandery, and Dongguan commandery was split off from Langya.
translations.idiomatic: At the same juncture Jin re-cut the Xiapi counties south of the Huai into a revived Linhuai commandery and peeled Dongguan off from Langya.

sentences.zh: 州凡領郡國七，縣六十一，戶八萬一千二十一。

sentences.zh: 七年，又分東莞置東安郡，分臨淮置淮陵郡，以堂邑置堂邑郡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again from Dongguan Dong'an commandery was split, from Linhuai Huailing commandery was split, and from Tangyi the Tangyi commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Jin's seventh Taikang year Jin carved Dong'an from Dongguan, Huailing from Linhuai, and spun Tangyi commandery out of the Tangyi district.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，臨淮、淮陵並淪沒石氏。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil, Linhuai and Huailing both sank and were lost to the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia's chaos swallowed both Linhuai and Huailing into Later Zhao's realm.

sentences.zh: 元帝渡江之後，徐州所得惟半，乃僑置淮陽、陽平、濟陰、北濟陰四郡。

translations.literal: After Yuan Emperor crossed the river, Xuzhou gained only half its former territory, so nominal commanderies of Huaiyang, Yangping, Jiyin, and Northern Jiyin were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Rui crossed the Yangzi, Jin held barely half the old Xuzhou ground, so refugee administrations called Huaiyang, Yangping, Jiyin, and Northern Jiyin were invented to hold the displaced.

sentences.zh: 又琅邪國人隨帝過江者，遂置懷德縣及琅邪郡以統之。

translations.literal: Again, people of the Langya kingdom who had followed the emperor across the river had Huaiyi county and the Langya commandery established to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Former subjects of the Langya kingdom who had trailed the court south received a new Huaiyi county and a shadow Langya commandery to keep their registers straight.

sentences.zh: 是時，幽、冀、青、并、兗五州及徐州之淮北流人相帥過江淮，帝並僑立郡縣以司牧之。

translations.literal: At this time, refugees from You, Ji, Qing, Bing, and Yan—the five provinces—and from north of the Huai in Xuzhou crossed the Jiang and Huai in bands, and the emperor altogether planted nominal commanderies and counties to shepherd them.
translations.idiomatic: You, Ji, Qing, Bing, and Yan, together with the Huai-north wing of Xuzhou, emptied onto the Yangzi and Huai in leaderless columns, and the throne answered by planting whole suites of nominal counties to govern exiles.

sentences.zh: 割吳郡之海虞北境，立郯、朐、利城、祝其、厚丘、西隰、襄賁七縣，寄居曲阿，以江乘置南東海、南琅邪、南東平、南蘭陵等郡，分武進立臨淮、淮陵、南彭城等郡，屬南徐州，又置頓丘郡屬北徐州。

translations.literal: He cut the northern fringe of Haiyu in Wu commandery to establish the seven counties Tan, Qu, Licheng, Zhuqi, Houqiu, Xixi, and Xiangben, lodging them at Qu'e; used Jiangcheng to establish Southern Donghai, Southern Langya, Southern Dongping, Southern Lanling, and other commanderies; split Wujin to establish Linhuai, Huailing, Southern Pengcheng, and other commanderies, belonging to southern Xuzhou; again established Dunqiu commandery belonging to northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin shaved Haiyu's north rim from Wu commandery to mint seven exile counties—Tan, Qu, Licheng, Zhuqi, Houqiu, Xixi, and Xiangben—parked them at Qu'e, stacked southern Donghai, Langya, Dongping, and Lanling commanderies on the old Jiangcheng belt, carved Linhuai, Huailing, and southern Pengcheng out of Wujin, folded them all under southern Xuzhou, and still spun up a Dunqiu commandery for northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明帝又立南沛、南清河、南下邳、南東莞、南平昌、南濟陰、南濮陽、南太平、南泰山、南濟陽、南魯等郡，以屬徐、兗二州，初或居江南，或居江北，或以兗州領州。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming again established Southern Pei, Southern Qinghe, Southern Xiapi, Southern Dongguan, Southern Pingchang, Southern Jiyin, Southern Puyang, Southern Taiping, Southern Mount Tai, Southern Jiyang, Southern Lu, and other commanderies, to belong to Xu and Yan provinces; at first some dwelt south of the Yangzi, some north of the river, or sometimes Yan province oversaw the province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming multiplied the paper jurisdictions—southern Pei, Qinghe, Xiapi, Dongguan, Pingchang, Jiyin, Puyang, Taiping, Tai, Jiyang, Lu, and more—split between Xu and Yan; some seats hugged the south bank, others the north, and sometimes a Yan governor held both titles at once.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒都督青兗二州諸軍事、兗州刺史，加領徐州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Xi Jian oversaw military affairs of Qing and Yan provinces, was governor of Yan, and additionally acting governor of Xuzhou, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian took overall command of Qing and Yan armies, kept the Yan governorship, added Xuzhou on an acting basis, and camped his headquarters at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻平後，自廣陵還鎮京口。

translations.literal: After Su Jun was suppressed, he returned from Guangling to be stationed at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Su Jun fell, Xi Jian pulled his headquarters from Guangling back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 又於漢故九江郡界置鐘離郡，屬南徐州，江北又僑立幽、冀、青、并四州。

translations.literal: Again within the bounds of Han's former Jiujiang commandery Zhongli commandery was set up, belonging to southern Xuzhou, and north of the river the four provinces You, Ji, Qing, and Bing were also planted in exile form.
translations.idiomatic: Inside old Han Jiujiang he chartered Zhongli commandery for southern Xuzhou, while north of the Yangzi he mirrored You, Ji, Qing, and Bing as phantom provinces for refugees.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，移南東海七縣出居京口。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu, the seven counties of southern Donghai were moved out to dwell at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu shifted the seven southern Donghai counties wholesale onto Jingkou.

sentences.zh: ，始分淮北為北徐州，淮南但為徐州，統彭城、沛、下邳、蘭陵、東莞、東安、琅邪、淮陽、陽平、濟陰、北濟陰十一郡，以盱眙立盱眙郡，統考城、直瀆、陽城三縣，又分廣陵界置海陵、山陽二郡。

translations.literal: , then north of the Huai was separately called Northern Xuzhou, while south of the Huai was simply Xuzhou, commanding the eleven commanderies Pengcheng, Pei, Xiapi, Lanling, Dongguan, Dong'an, Langya, Huaiyang, Yangping, Jiyin, and Northern Jiyin; Xuyi commandery was established at Xuyi, commanding Kaocheng, Zhidu, and Yangcheng counties; again within Guangling's bounds Hailing and Shanyang commanderies were split off.
translations.idiomatic: , after which ground north of the Huai was labeled northern Xuzhou, the Huai-south rump kept the plain name Xuzhou, and that rump still listed eleven heartland commanderies; a new Xuyi commandery sat at Xuyi with three attendant counties; Guangling meanwhile yielded Hailing and Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 後又以幽冀合徐州，青并合兗州。

translations.literal: Later You and Ji were merged into Xuzhou, Qing and Bing merged into Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court folded You and Ji into Xuzhou while Qing and Bing were absorbed into Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 案《禹貢》荊及衡陽之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。

translations.literal: According to the 《Yu Gong》, this is the land of Jing and the region south of Mount Heng; of Shun's twelve shepherds, it was one.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Tribute of Yu》 sketches this belt as "Jing" and the country south of Mount Heng—one of the twelve domains Shun placed under pasture chiefs.

translations.literal: The 《Zhou Li》: "The due south is called Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》 calls the southern quadrant "Jingzhou."

translations.literal: " The 《Chunqiu Yuanming Bao》 says: "The Winnowing Basket constellation scatters and becomes Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The apocryphon 《Yuanming Bao》 maps the Winnowing Basket asterism onto Jingzhou.

translations.literal: " "Jing" means strong; it says its qi is rash and strong.
translations.idiomatic: " The graph jing means "hard"; commentators read that as brash, forceful energy.

sentences.zh: 亦曰警也，言南蠻數為寇逆，其人有道後服，無道先強，常警備也。

translations.literal: Also it is called "alert"; it means the southern Man often acted as bandits and rebels, their people, if the ruler had the Way submitted afterward, if without the Way grew strong first—they were constantly alert and prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Others gloss jing as "watchful," because southern tribes raided often: when a court had virtue they came late to allegiance, when it lacked virtue they struck first, so the heartland kept its guard up.

translations.literal: Again it says the name was taken from Mount Jing.
translations.idiomatic: A third etymology simply ties the name to Mount Jing itself.

translations.literal: During the Warring States, its territory was Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Warring States age the whole basin belonged to Chu.

sentences.zh: 及秦，取楚鄢郢為南郡，又取巫中地為黔中郡，以楚之漢北立南陽郡，滅楚之後，分黔中為長沙郡。

translations.literal: When Qin took Chu's Yan and Ying and made the Southern (Nan) commandery, again took Wuzhong lands as Qianzhong commandery, established Nanyang commandery from Chu's territory north of the Han River, and after destroying Chu split Qianzhong into Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin seized Yan and Ying to form the southern capital commandery, carved the Wushan midstream into Qianzhong, lifted Nanyang from Chu's Han-north marches, then split Qianzhong into Changsha once Chu fell.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖分長沙為桂陽郡，改黔中為武陵郡，分南郡為江夏郡。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu split Changsha to make Guiyang commandery, changed Qianzhong to Wuling commandery, split Nan commandery to make Jiangxia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu peeled Guiyang out of Changsha, renamed Qianzhong as Wuling, and sliced Jiangxia from Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 武帝又分長沙為零陵郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu again split Changsha to make Lingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han later hived Lingling away from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 及置十三州，因舊名為荊州，統南郡、南陽、零陵、桂陽、武陵、長沙、江夏七郡。

translations.literal: When the thirteen provinces were established, following the old name it was called Jingzhou, commanding the seven commanderies Nan, Nanyang, Lingling, Guiyang, Wuling, Changsha, and Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Han drew thirteen provinces, the old Chu core kept the name Jingzhou and bundled Nan, Nanyang, Lingling, Guiyang, Wuling, Changsha, and Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 後漢獻帝，魏武盡得荊州之地，分南郡以北立襄陽郡，又分南陽西界立南鄉郡，分枝江以西立臨江郡。

translations.literal: Under Later Han's Emperor Xian, Cao Cao of Wei gained the whole of Jingzhou, split off north of Nan commandery to establish Xiangyang commandery, again split the western border of Nanyang to establish Nanxiang commandery, and split west of Zhijiang to establish Linjiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xian's reign Cao Cao seized every Jingzhou circuit: he lifted Xiangyang from the Nan commandery north bank, carved Nanxiang from Nanyang's west edge, and drew Linjiang from the lands west of Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 及敗于赤壁，南郡以南屬吳，吳後遂與蜀分荊州。

translations.literal: When he was defeated at Chibi, south of Nan commandery belonged to Wu, and Wu later divided Jingzhou with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Red Cliffs debacle everything south of Nan commandery slid to Wu, and Wu soon split the province down the middle with Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是南郡、零陵、武陵以西為蜀，江夏、桂陽、長沙三郡為吳，南陽、襄陽、南鄉三郡為魏。

translations.literal: Thereupon west of Nan, Lingling, and Wuling was Shu; the three commanderies Jiangxia, Guiyang, and Changsha were Wu; the three commanderies Nanyang, Xiangyang, and Nanxiang were Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The partition left Shu with the Nan–Lingling–Wuling west, Wu with Jiangxia, Guiyang, and Changsha, and Wei with Nanyang, Xiangyang, and Nanxiang.

translations.literal: Thus the name Jingzhou stood in duplicate north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Hence two different realms each flew the old name Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀分南郡，立宜都郡，劉備沒後，宜都、武陵、零陵、南郡四郡之地悉復屬吳。

translations.literal: Shu split Nan commandery to establish Yidu commandery; after Liu Bei died, the lands of Yidu, Wuling, Lingling, and Nan commanderies all again belonged to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had cut Yidu out of Nan, but once Liu Bei was gone Wu reclaimed Yidu together with Wuling, Lingling, and the Nan heartland.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝以漢中遺黎立魏興、新城二郡，明帝分新城立上庸郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei used remaining people of Hanzhong to establish Weixing and Xincheng commanderies; Emperor Ming split Xincheng to establish Shangyong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi settled Hanzhong holdouts into Weixing and Xincheng; Mingdi later split Xincheng again to seat Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 孫權分江夏立武昌郡，又分蒼梧立臨賀郡，分長沙立衡陽、湘東二郡。

translations.literal: Sun Quan split Jiangxia to establish Wuchang commandery, again split Cangwu to establish Linhe commandery, split Changsha to establish Hengyang and Xiangdong commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan spun Wuchang out of Jiangxia, Linhe out of Cangwu, and both Hengyang and Xiangdong out of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 孫休分武陵立天門郡，分宜都立建平郡。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu split Wuling to establish Tianmen commandery, split Yidu to establish Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu added Tianmen from Wuling and Jianping from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 孫皓分零陵立始安郡，分桂陽立始興郡，又分零陵立邵陵郡，分長沙立安成郡。

translations.literal: Sun Hao split Lingling to establish Shi'an commandery, split Guiyang to establish Shixing commandery, again split Lingling to establish Shaoling commandery, split Changsha to establish Ancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao busied the map further: Shi'an and Shaoling from Lingling, Shixing from Guiyang, Ancheng from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 荊州統南郡、武昌、武陵、宜都、建平、天門、長沙、零陵、桂陽、衡陽、湘東、邵陵、臨賀、始興、始安十五郡，其南陽、江夏、襄陽、南鄉、魏興、新城、上庸七郡屬魏之荊州。

translations.literal: Jingzhou commanded fifteen commanderies—Nan, Wuchang, Wuling, Yidu, Jianping, Tianmen, Changsha, Lingling, Guiyang, Hengyang, Xiangdong, Shaoling, Linhe, Shixing, and Shi'an; the seven commanderies Nanyang, Jiangxia, Xiangyang, Nanxiang, Weixing, Xincheng, and Shangyong belonged to Wei's Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's Jingzhou roster ran to fifteen commanderies, while Wei kept a parallel stack of seven—Nanyang, Jiangxia, Xiangyang, Nanxiang, Weixing, Xincheng, and Shangyong—under its own Jingzhou label.

sentences.zh: 及武帝平吳，分南郡為南平郡，分南陽立義陽郡，改南鄉順陽郡，又以始興、始安、臨賀三郡屬廣州，以揚州之安成郡來屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Wu, he split Nan commandery to make Nanping commandery, split Nanyang to establish Yiyang commandery, changed Nanxiang to Shunyang commandery, again subordinated Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe to Guangzhou, and brought Ancheng commandery from Yangzhou into Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin conquered Wu, Sima Yan split Nan into Nanping, raised Yiyang from Nanyang, renamed Nanxiang as Shunyang, reassigned Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe to Guangzhou, and pulled Yangzhou's Ancheng back under Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 惠帝分桂陽、武昌、安成三郡立江州，以新城、魏興、上庸三郡屬梁州，又分義陽立隨郡，分南陽立新野郡，分江夏立竟陵郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui split Guiyang, Wuchang, and Ancheng—three commanderies—to establish Jiangzhou, subordinated Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong—three commanderies—to Liangzhou, again split Yiyang to establish Sui commandery, split Nanyang to establish Xinye commandery, and split Jiangxia to establish Jingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui spun Jiangzhou out of Guiyang, Wuchang, and Ancheng, handed the Hanzhong spillway commanderies to Liangzhou, added Sui, Xinye, and Jingling as still more splinters.

sentences.zh: 懷帝又分長沙、衡陽、湘東、零陵、邵陵、桂陽及廣州之始安、始興、臨賀九郡置湘州。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai again split Changsha, Hengyang, Xiangdong, Lingling, Shaoling, Guiyang, and from Guangzhou Shi'an, Shixing, and Linhe—nine commanderies—to establish Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai declared a new Xiangzhou built from nine southern circuits, borrowing three cantons from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀亂，又割南郡之華容、州陵、監利三縣別立豐都，合四縣置成都郡，為成都王穎國，居華容縣。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was in turmoil, again Huarong, Zhouling, and Jianli—three counties of Nan commandery—were cut off separately to establish Fengdu, and together four counties were placed as Chengdu commandery, becoming the state of Prince Chengdu Sima Ying, dwelling at Huarong county.
translations.idiomatic: While Shu convulsed, Jin carved Huarong, Zhouling, and Jianli out of Nan commandery, invented a fourth seat called Fengdu, bundled them into a paper Chengdu commandery for Sima Ying, and parked the whole fiction at Huarong.

sentences.zh: 愍帝建興中，並還南郡，亦併豐都於監利。

translations.literal: In Emperor Min's Jianxing era, they were merged back into Nan commandery, and Fengdu was also merged into Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min the patchwork was folded back into Nan commandery, and the empty Fengdu county vanished into Jianli.

sentences.zh: 元帝渡江，又僑立新興、南河東二郡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Emperor crossed the river, again nominal Xinxing and Southern Hedong—two commanderies—were established.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Rui crossed the Yangzi, refugee registers added Xinxing and southern Hedong.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，又分零陵立營陽郡，以義陽流人在南郡者立為義陽郡。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu, again Yingyang commandery was split from Lingling, and Yiyang commandery was established for Yiyang refugees who were in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu peeled Yingyang from Lingling and pasted a new Yiyang commandery over river exiles stranded in Nan.

sentences.zh: 又以廣州之臨賀、始興、始安三郡及江州之桂陽，益州之巴東，合五郡來屬，以長沙、衡陽、湘東、零陵、邵陵、營陽六郡屬湘州。

translations.literal: Again Linhe, Shixing, and Shi'an—three commanderies of Guangzhou—together with Guiyang of Jiangzhou and Badong of Yizhou—five commanderies in all—came to belong; Changsha, Hengyang, Xiangdong, Lingling, Shaoling, and Yingyang—six commanderies—belonged to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three Guangzhou prefectures, Guiyang from Jiangzhou, and Badong from Shu were reassigned to Jingzhou, while six lake circuits were handed to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 桓溫又分南郡立武寧郡。

translations.literal: Huan Wen again split Nan commandery to establish Wuning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sliced Wuning out of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 安帝又僑立南義陽、東義陽、長寧三郡。

translations.literal: Emperor An again nominally established Southern Yiyang, Eastern Yiyang, and Changning—three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An added three more paper Yiyangs and a Changning for refugees.

sentences.zh: ，省湘州，長沙、衡陽、湘東、零陵、邵陵、營陽還入荊州。

translations.idiomatic: , then Xiangzhou was dropped and its six counties flowed back under Jingzhou.

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou": "The southeast is called Yangzhou.

translations.literal: " The "Yuanming Bao of the Spring and Autumn Annals" says: "The Ox Lead flows and becomes Yangzhou, dividing into the Yue state.
translations.idiomatic: " The apocryphon "Yuanming Bao" ties the Ox Lead asterism to Yangzhou and the old Yue southlands.

sentences.zh: 」以為江南之氣躁勁，厥性輕揚。

translations.literal: " They considered that south of the Yangzi the qi is rash and sharp, its nature light and buoyant.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentators describe Jiangnan qi as restless, sharp, and buoyant."

sentences.zh: 亦曰，州界多水，水波揚也。

translations.literal: Also it is said: within the province's bounds there is much water, and water waves rise.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss cites the endless rivers—the very waves that make the land feel "lifted."

sentences.zh: 于古則荒服之國，戰國時其地為楚分。

translations.literal: In antiquity it was a wild-domain state; in Warring States its territory was a partition of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently it counted as outer wilds; by the Warring States age Chu had swallowed every march.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇併天下，以置鄣、會稽、九江三郡。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang united the realm and thereby established the three commanderies of Zhang, Kuaiji, and Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang organized the southeast as Zhang, Kuaiji, and Jiujiang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 項羽封英布為九江王，盡有其地。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu enfeoffed Ying Bu as king of Jiujiang, and he wholly possessed its territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu gave Ying Bu the whole Jiujiang basin as his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 漢改九江曰淮南，即封布為淮南王。

translations.literal: Han changed Jiujiang to Huainan and thereupon enfeoffed Bu as king of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Han renamed Jiujiang Huainan and let Bu keep the same ground under the new title.

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Huainan was split to establish Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Han's sixth year Gaozu peeled Yuzhang out of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，布誅，立皇子長為淮南王，封劉濞為吳王，二國盡得揚州之地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Bu was executed; an imperial son, Chang, was established as king of Huainan, and Liu Pi was enfeoffed as king of Wu—the two kingdoms wholly obtained Yangzhou's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years in, Bu died; Liu Chang took Huainan while Liu Pi took Wu, together holding every Yangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 文帝十六年，分淮南立廬江、衡山二郡。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's sixteenth year, Huainan was split to establish Lujiang and Hengshan—two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen split Huainan again into Lujiang and Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 景帝四年，封皇子非為江都王，並得鄣、會稽郡，而不得豫章。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's fourth year, an imperial son, Fei, was enfeoffed as king of Jiangdu, and together obtained Zhang and Kuaiji commanderies, but did not obtain Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing gave Prince Fei Jiangdu plus Zhang and Kuaiji, but withheld Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 武帝改江都曰廣陵，封皇子胥為王而以屬徐州。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu changed Jiangdu to Guangling, enfeoffed an imperial son, Xu, as king, and subordinated it to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu renamed Jiangdu Guangling, made it Prince Xu's fief, and shifted it under Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: ，改鄣曰丹楊，改淮南復為九江。

translations.literal: , Zhang was changed to Danyang, and Huainan was again changed to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: , then Zhang became Danyang while Huainan reverted to the Jiujiang label.

sentences.zh: 後漢順帝分會稽立吳郡，揚州統會稽、丹楊、吳、豫章、九江、廬江六郡，省六安併廬江郡。

translations.literal: Later Han's Emperor Shun split Kuaiji to establish Wu commandery; Yangzhou commanded Kuaiji, Danyang, Wu, Yuzhang, Jiujiang, and Lujiang—six commanderies—and abolished Lu'an, merging it into Lujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun of Later Han cut Wu out of Kuaiji; Yangzhou now ran six commanderies and swallowed Lu'an into Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 獻帝興平中，孫策分豫章立廬陵郡。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xian's Xingping era, Sun Ce split Yuzhang to establish Luling commandery.

translations.literal: , Xunyang and Chaisang—two counties of Lujiang and Wuchang—were split to establish Xunyang commandery, belonging to Jiangzhou, and Wujiang and Liyang—two counties of Huainan—were split to establish Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: , then Xunyang and Chaisang were paired into a new Xunyang commandery under Jiangzhou, while Wujiang and Liyang became a fresh Liyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 又以周玘創義討石冰，割吳興之陽羨並長城縣之北鄉置義鄉、國山、臨津並陽羨四縣，又分丹陽之永世置平陵及永世，凡六縣，立義興郡，以表紀之功，並屬揚州。

translations.literal: Again because Zhou Qi raised loyal troops to attack Shi Bing, Yangxian of Wuxing together with the northern township of Changcheng county were cut to establish the four counties Yixiang, Guoshan, Linjin, and Yangxian, again Yongshi of Danyang was split to establish Pingling and Yongshi—six counties in all—and Yixing commandery was established to mark Zhou's merit; all belonged to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhou Qi had led loyalists against Shi Bing, Jin carved Yixing from Yangxian and Changcheng's north township, split Danyang's Yongshi into Pingling, and bundled six counties into a new Yixing commandery to honor him—all still under Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以毗陵郡封東海王世子毗，避毗諱，改為晉陵。

translations.literal: Again because the Piling commandery was enfeoffed on the heir of the Prince of Donghai, Pi, avoiding the taboo on pi, it was changed to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Donghai's heir received Piling as a fief, the name was tabooed to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 懷帝，又以豫章之彭澤縣屬尋陽郡。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huai, again Pengze county of Yuzhang was subordinated to Xunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai shifted Pengze from Yuzhang into Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 愍帝立，避帝諱改建鄴為建康。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended, avoiding the imperial taboo Jianye was changed to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min renamed Jianye Jiankang to honor his own taboo.

sentences.zh: 元帝渡江，建都揚州，改丹陽太守為尹，江州又置新蔡郡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Emperor crossed the river, he established his capital at Yangzhou, changed the governor of Danyang to a yin metropolitan governor, and Jiangzhou again established Xincai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui made Yangzhou his capital circuit, promoted Danyang's governor to yin, and let Jiangzhou add Xincai.

sentences.zh: 尋陽郡又置九江、上甲二縣，尋又省九江縣入尋陽。

translations.literal: Xunyang commandery again established Jiujiang and Shangjia—two counties—soon again abolished Jiujiang county, merging it into Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang briefly listed Jiujiang and Shangjia, then folded Jiujiang back into the mother county.

sentences.zh: 是時司、冀、雍、涼、青、并、兗、豫、幽、平諸州皆淪沒，江南所得但有揚、荊、湘、江、梁、益、交、廣，其徐州則有過半，豫州惟得譙城而已。

translations.literal: At this time Si, Ji, Yong, Liang, Qing, Bing, Yan, Yu, You, Ping—all these provinces—were lost; what the south of the Yangzi obtained was only Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiang, Liang, Yi, Jiao, and Guang; as for Xuzhou it had a little more than half, and Yuzhou obtained only Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: North China's dozen provinces had fallen; the court held only the eight southern ones plus fragments of Xu and a Qiao enclave masquerading as Yu.

sentences.zh: 明帝，分臨海立永嘉郡，流永甯、安固、松陽、橫陽等四縣，而揚州統丹陽、吳郡、吳興、新安、東陽、臨海、永嘉、宣城、義興、晉陵十一郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming split Linhai to establish Yongjia commandery, transferring Yongning, Angu, Songyang, and Hengyang—four counties—and Yangzhou commanded Danyang, Wu, Wuxing, Xin'an, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yixing, and Jinling—eleven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming cut Yongjia from Linhai and moved four coast counties under it, leaving Yangzhou with eleven commanderies on the books.

sentences.zh: 自中原亂離，遺黎南渡，並僑置牧司在廣陵，丹徒南城，非舊土也。

translations.literal: From the Central Plain's turmoil and separation, surviving people crossed south, and altogether nominal shepherds were planted at Guangling and the south city of Dantu—not their old soil.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees stacked nominal governors at Guangling and Dantu's south gate—nowhere near their true northland homes.

sentences.zh: 及胡寇南侵，淮南百姓皆渡江。

translations.literal: When Hu raiders invaded south, the common people of Huainan all crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Each Hu thrust emptied Huainan onto the south bank.

sentences.zh: 成帝初，蘇峻、祖約為亂于江淮，胡寇又大至，百姓南渡者轉多，乃於江南僑立淮南郡及諸縣，又于尋陽僑置松滋郡，遙隸揚州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Cheng, Su Jun and Zu Yue made turmoil in the Jiang and Huai; Hu raiders again came in great force, and the common people who crossed south grew ever more numerous; thereupon south of the Yangzi nominal Huainan commandery and various counties were planted, and again at Xunyang nominal Songzi commandery was placed, remotely subordinate to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Cheng's reign Su Jun and Zu Yue wrecked the Huai line, fresh invasions followed, and Jin papered the south with shadow Huainan and a distant Songzi commandery seated at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，僑置魏郡、廣川、高陽、堂邑等諸郡，並所統縣並寄居京邑，改陵陽為廣陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang, nominal Wei, Guangchuan, Gaoyang, Tangyi, and other commanderies were planted, and the counties they commanded altogether lodged in the capital district; Lingyang was changed to Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 4 brought a raft of phantom northern commanderies packed around the capital, while Lingyang was retitled Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武，又分永嘉郡之永甯縣置樂成縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu again split Yongning county of Yongjia commandery to establish Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu peeled Lecheng out of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 是時上党百姓南渡，僑立上黨郡為四縣，寄居蕪湖。

translations.literal: At this time the common people of Shangdang crossed south, and nominal Shangdang commandery was established as four counties, lodged at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang exiles gained a paper commandery of four counties parked at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 尋又省上黨郡為縣，又罷襄城郡為繁昌縣，並以屬淮南。

translations.literal: Soon again Shangdang commandery was abolished to be a county, and Xiangcheng commandery was abolished to be Fanchang county, both belonging to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Later the phantom Shangdang shrank to a single county, Xiangcheng collapsed into Fanchang, and both sat under Huainan.

sentences.zh: 安帝，省尋陽縣入柴桑縣，柴桑仍為郡，後又省上甲縣入彭澤縣。

translations.literal: Emperor An abolished Xunyang county into Chaisang county, Chaisang still remained a commandery, later again abolished Shangjia county into Pengze county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An swallowed Xunyang into Chaisang, kept Chaisang as a commandery seat, and later merged Shangjia into Pengze.

sentences.zh: 舊江州督荊州之竟陵郡，及何無忌為刺史，表以竟陵去州遼遠，去江陵三百里，荊州所立綏安郡人戶入境，欲資此郡助江濱戍防，以竟陵郡還荊州。

translations.literal: Formerly Jiangzhou supervised Jingzhou's Jingling commandery, and when He Wuji became inspector, he memorialized that because Jingling was far from the province—three hundred li from Jiangling—and the people and households of Sui'an commandery established by Jingzhou had entered its territory, wishing to rely on this commandery to assist riverbank garrison defense, Jingling commandery was returned to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou once oversaw Jingling until He Wuji argued it belonged with Jingzhou proper once Sui'an settlers spilled across the border.

sentences.zh: 又司州之弘農、揚州之松滋二郡寄在尋陽，人戶難居，並宜建督。

translations.literal: Again Hongnong of Si province and Songzi of Yang province—two commanderies—were lodged at Xunyang, and the people and households were hard to dwell together; both ought to have a supervisor established.
translations.idiomatic: Exile versions of Hongnong and Songzi overlapped at Xunyang, so officials begged for a dedicated overseer.

translations.literal: Emperor An followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 後又省松滋郡為松滋縣，弘農郡為弘農縣，並屬尋陽郡。

translations.literal: Later again Songzi commandery was abolished to be Songzi county, and Hongnong commandery to be Hongnong county, both belonging to Xunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later both phantom commanderies devolved to counties inside Xunyang.

translations.literal: Jiao province
translations.idiomatic: Jiao province

sentences.zh: 案《禹貢》揚州之域，是為南越之土。

translations.literal: According to the "Tribute of Yu," this is Yangzhou's territory; it is the soil of the southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" counts the Red River basin as part of Yangzhou—the old Yue southlands.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇即略定揚越，以謫戍卒五十萬人守五嶺。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang thereupon pacified Yang Yue and used fifty thousand exiled garrison soldiers to guard the Five Ranges.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor seized the Yue hills and parked fifty thousand penal troops on the five passes.

sentences.zh: 自北徂南，入越之道，必由嶺嶠，時有五處，故曰五嶺。

translations.literal: From north going south, the roads into Yue necessarily pass the range cols; at that time there were five places, hence they are called the Five Ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Every road south climbed a ridge saddle—five of them, hence the name Five Ranges.

sentences.zh: 後使任囂、趙他攻越，略取陸梁地，遂定南越，以為桂林、南海、象等三郡，非三十六郡之限，乃置南海尉以典之，所謂東南一尉也。

translations.literal: Later he sent Ren Xiao and Zhao Tuo to attack Yue, seized the Luliang uplands, thereupon pacified Southern Yue, and made Guilin, Nanhai, Xiang, and other three commanderies—not within the limit of the thirty-six commanderies—thereupon established a Nanhai commandant to oversee them, the so-called "southeastern single commandant."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiao and Zhao Tuo stormed the Luliang hills, carved Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang outside Qin's thirty-sixfold map, and invented a Nanhai commandant—the "one commandant of the southeast."

sentences.zh: 漢初，以嶺南三郡及長沙、豫章封吳芮為長沙王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, the three Lingnan commanderies together with Changsha and Yuzhang were enfeoffed on Wu Rui as king of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han let Wu Rui keep Lingnan plus Changsha and Yuzhang as his Changsha kingdom.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以南武侯織為南海王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Marquis of Nanwu Zhi was made king of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Gaozu ennobled the Nanwu marquis as king of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 陸賈使還，拜趙他為南越王，割長沙之南三郡以封之。

translations.literal: When Lu Jia returned from his mission, Zhao Tuo was appointed king of Southern Yue, and the three southern commanderies of Changsha were cut to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia's embassy ended with Zhao Tuo as Southern Yue king, funded by three southern Changsha commanderies.

sentences.zh: 武帝，討平呂嘉，以其地為南海、蒼梧、郁林、合浦、日南、九真、交趾七郡，蓋秦時三郡之地。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, punishing and pacifying Lü Jia, took its territory as Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Rinan, Jiuzhen, and Jiaozhi—seven commanderies—covering the territory of Qin's three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi crushed Lü Jia and drew seven commanderies—roughly Qin's triple Lingnan map.

sentences.zh: 元封中，又置儋耳、珠崖二郡，置交趾刺史以督之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era, again Dan'er and Zhuya—two commanderies—were established, and a Jiaozhi inspector was placed to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng added Hainan's Dan'er and Zhuya plus a roaming Jiaozhi inspector.

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao abolished Dan'er, merging it into Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao folded Dan'er into Zhuya.

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan again abolished Zhuya commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan dropped Zhuya altogether.

sentences.zh: 後漢馬援平定交部，始調立城郭置井邑。

translations.literal: Later Han's Ma Yuan pacified the Jiao region and thereupon began to adjust and establish walls and towns and set wells and settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan's Later Han campaign finally ringed the Red River plain with walls and wells.

sentences.zh: 順帝，交趾太守周敞求立為州，朝議不許，即拜敞為交趾刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun—Jiaozhi governor Zhou Chang requested to establish a province; court deliberation did not grant it, but thereupon Zhou Chang was appointed Jiaozhi inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Chang begged for provincial status and had to settle for inspector.

sentences.zh: 桓帝分立高興郡，靈帝改曰高涼。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan separately established Gaoxing commandery; Emperor Ling changed it to Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan split Gaoxing from the coast; Ling renamed it Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: ，張津為刺史，士燮交趾太守，共表立為州，乃拜津為交州牧。

translations.literal: , Zhang Jin became inspector, Shi Xie was Jiaozhi governor, and together they memorialized to establish a province; thereupon Zhang Jin was appointed Jiao provincial shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: , then Zhang Jin and Shi Xie jointly won imperial approval for a real province, and Zhang Jin took the shepherd's staff.

sentences.zh: 十五年，移居番禺，詔以邊州使持節，郡給鼓吹，以重城鎮，加以九錫六佾之舞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he moved his residence to Panyu; an edict ordered that border provinces use the staff of authority, commanderies be given processional music, to emphasize the great garrison, and in addition grant the nine bestowals and the six-row dance.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years on the seat shifted to Panyu with full border-province honors—processional bands, nine tins, six rows of dancers.

sentences.zh: 吳，割南海、蒼梧、郁林三郡立廣州，交趾、日南、九真、合浦四郡為交州。

translations.literal: Wu split Nanhai, Cangwu, and Yulin—three commanderies—to establish Guang province; Jiaozhi, Rinan, Jiuzhen, and Hepu—four commanderies—became Jiao province.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu peeled Guangzhou from three eastern Lingnan commanderies while the four western ones stayed Jiao.

sentences.zh: 戴良為刺史，值亂不得入，呂岱擊平之，復還併交部。

translations.literal: Dai Liang became inspector; encountering turmoil he could not enter; Lü Dai attacked and pacified it, again returned and merged the Jiao region.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Liang could not reach his post until Lü Dai cleared the roads and reunited the inspectorate.

translations.literal: , Zhuya commandery was again established.
translations.idiomatic: , and Wu briefly revived Zhuya.

translations.literal: , again the former three commanderies were used to establish Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: , then re-split the eastern trio into Guangzhou once more.

sentences.zh: 及孫皓，又立新昌、武平、九德三郡。

translations.literal: By Sun Hao, again Xinchang, Wuping, and Jiude—three commanderies—were newly established.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao added Xinchang, Wuping, and Jiude.

sentences.zh: 蜀以李恢為建甯太守，遙領交州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu appointed Li Hui as Jianning governor, concurrently overseeing Jiao inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Shu made Li Hui Jianning governor with a paper Jiao portfolio.

sentences.zh: 晉平蜀，以蜀建甯太守霍弋遙領交州，得以便宜選用長吏。

translations.literal: When Jin pacified Shu, Shu's Jianning governor Huo Yi concurrently oversaw Jiao province and was able at convenience to select and appoint senior clerks.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, Huo Yi kept the same remote Jiao title with discretionary hiring.

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, Zhuya was abolished into Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu collapsed, Jin merged Zhuya into Hepu.

sentences.zh: 交州統郡七，縣五十三，戶二萬五千六百。

translations.literal: Jiao province commanded seven commanderies, fifty-three counties, and twenty-five thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Reunified Jiao province listed seven commanderies, 53 counties, and 25,600 households.

translations.idiomatic: The Red River delta counties ran from Longbian and Goulou through Wanghai and the twin-graph Mengxie seat, then Xiyu, Wuning, Zhu yuan, Qu yang, Jiao xing, Beidai, Jixu, Anding, Nanding, and Haiping.

translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen commandery

translations.idiomatic: 〈Wu organized the old Yuechang country of Zhou legend.

translations.literal: It commands eight counties and has no households [record].〉
translations.idiomatic: It listed eight counties but no reliable household tally.〉

translations.idiomatic: 〈South of Xianglin lay four kingdoms whose elites claimed Han descent; Han had raised bronze pillars here to mark the frontier.

translations.idiomatic: Guang province

sentences.zh: 案《禹貢》揚州之域，秦末趙他所據之地。

translations.literal: According to the "Tribute of Yu," this is Yangzhou's territory; it is the land Zhao Tuo held at the end of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" still counts the Pearl River mouth as Yangzhou—the belt Zhao Tuo seized when Qin collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及漢武帝，以其地為交址郡。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Wu of Han, he took its territory as Jiaozhi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi folded the same ground into Jiaozhi commandery.

sentences.zh: 至吳，分交州之南海、蒼梧、郁林、高梁四郡立為廣州，俄復舊。

translations.literal: By Wu, Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, and Gaoliang—four commanderies of Jiao province—were split to establish Guang province; soon it reverted to the old arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu briefly declared Guangzhou from four eastern Jiao commanderies, then reversed the split.

sentences.zh: ，復分交州置廣州，分合浦立合浦北部，以都尉領之。

translations.literal: , again Jiao province was split to establish Guang province, Hepu was split to establish northern Hepu, led by a commandant.
translations.idiomatic: , later Wu split Guangzhou off again and added a northern Hepu commandant's district.

translations.literal: Sun Hao split Yulin to establish Guilin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao carved Guilin out of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 及太康中，吳平，遂以荊州始安、始興、臨賀三郡來屬。

translations.literal: By the Taikang era, when Wu was pacified, thereupon Shi'an, Shixing, and Linhe—three commanderies of Jingzhou—came to belong.

sentences.zh: 成帝分南海立東官郡，以始興、臨賀二郡還屬荊州。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng split Nanhai to establish Dongguan commandery, and Shixing and Linhe—two commanderies—were returned to belong to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng added Dongguan from Nanhai but sent Shixing and Linhe back to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆帝分蒼梧立晉康、新甯、永平三郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu split Cangwu to establish Jinkang, Xinning, and Yongping—three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu cut Jinkang, Xinning, and Yongping out of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 哀帝太和中置新安郡，安帝分東官立義安郡，恭帝分南海立新會郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai, in the Taihe years, established Xin'an commandery; Emperor An split Dongguan to establish Yi'an commandery; Emperor Gong split Nanhai to establish Xinhui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai chartered Xin'an, Emperor An spun Yi'an from Dongguan, and Emperor Gong hived Xinhui off Nanhai.
